briefing.text: Promoter mutations are non-coding. In a MAF they appear as Variant_Classification 5'Flank (sometimes 5'UTR or IGR) with Consequence upstream_gene_variant, and they have no HGVSp. Do not filter data_mutations.txt to nonsynonymous classes or rely on protein changes when looking for NFKBIE promoter mutations. Tabulate Variant_Classification, Consequence and Start_Position for every NFKBIE-related row first.
briefing.reason: A standard coding-only filter would remove every promoter variant, and the result would look like 'absent'.

briefing.text: NFKBIE (chr6p21.1, roughly chr6:44.225-44.233 Mb in GRCh37; check NCBI_Build) is on the minus strand. Its promoter/TSS is therefore at the HIGHER-coordinate end of the gene, not below the start coordinate. Look for promoter variants by coordinate window (about 2 kb around the TSS of canonical transcript ENST00000275015) as well as by gene name. Promoter variants may be annotated to a neighbouring gene's Hugo_Symbol, carry Entrez_Gene_Id 0, or name NFKBIE only in SYMBOL/all_effects, so search those columns case-insensitively. Note whether hits recur at the same position and whether they are UV-type C>T/CC>TT changes.
briefing.reason: Searching the wrong side of the gene, or matching Hugo_Symbol=='NFKBIE' exactly, can miss real promoter calls.

briefing.text: The hypothesis is about desmoplastic melanoma specifically. Join Tumor_Sample_Barcode to SAMPLE_ID in data_clinical_sample.txt, restrict to desmoplastic samples (ONCOTREE_CODE / CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED), and report counts separately for pure and mixed desmoplastic histology if a histology-category column exists.
briefing.reason: Counting across the whole mutation file without the subtype restriction can mislabel the result.

briefing.text: 'Absent' is a universal claim. One credible somatic NFKBIE promoter mutation in a desmoplastic sample contradicts it. Zero hits supports it only if the promoter region was actually assayed. If no hits are found, check whether the mutation file contains any non-coding calls at all (5'Flank/upstream/IGR) and what sequencing applies to the samples (e.g. whole genome vs exome/panel). If the promoter was not covered, the absence of calls is uninformative.
briefing.reason: This decides how the result maps to a label: hits, zero hits with coverage, or zero hits without coverage lead to different conclusions.

briefing.text: Non-coding calls are enriched for germline polymorphisms and artefacts. For any candidate NFKBIE promoter rows, inspect dbSNP_RS, population allele frequencies (GMAF/ExAC_AF), Mutation_Status, FILTER and VAF (t_alt_count/t_depth). Exclude common polymorphisms (population AF >1%) and weakly supported calls. The same position recurring across samples is evidence of a real somatic hotspot.
briefing.reason: Without this check, a germline SNP or artefact could wrongly be counted as a promoter mutation that contradicts the hypothesis.

shared_assumptions: Both teams count the recurring chr6:44233400 C>T variant (plus the CC>TT next to it) at the 5' end of NFKBIE as an 'NFKBIE promoter mutation'. On the canonical transcript, though, it is annotated as a coding missense change (c.101G>A p.G34E). Only team B relied on the upstream_gene_variant annotation of a non-canonical transcript. Neither team used the data to check where the variant sits relative to the transcription start site or promoter (e.g. DISTANCE, cDNA_position, BIOTYPE of ENST00000477930).
Both assume the recurring C>T calls are real somatic mutations, not artefacts or germline variants, without checking read support or the filter and validation flags for each call.

Both assume a promoter variant could have been detected equally well in all 20 samples. The PLATFORM field says 'Exome, Whole Genome', and neither team looked at Sequence_Source for each call, so whether the locus was covered in every sample was never checked.
unused_evidence: MAF columns DISTANCE, Feature, Feature_type, BIOTYPE, cDNA_position, CANONICAL, MOTIF_NAME/MOTIF_SCORE_CHANGE: these could show how far the hotspot is from the start of the alternative transcript, whether that transcript codes for protein, and whether a regulatory-feature annotation exists. All of this bears directly on the 'promoter' label.

FILTER, Mutation_Status, Validation_Status, Verification_Status, Validation_Method, t_alt_count/t_depth, n_alt_count/n_depth: evidence on the quality and somatic status of the NFKBIE hits. Neither team reported these.
Sequence_Source and Sequencing_Phase for each call, and PLATFORM/SECONDARY_PLATFORM for each sample: these could show whether the NFKBIE hits, and any absence of hits, come from exome or genome data.

HISTOLOGICAL_SUBTYPE (Neurotropic/Not Seen, per patient) and DETAILED_SAMPLE_HISTOLOGY_CATEGORY (Pure/Mixed, per sample): team A split pure from mixed, but team B did not say whether its hits fall in pure desmoplastic melanoma.
unresolved_weak_points: Team A named this as its weakest point: the hotspot is annotated as coding, so calling it a promoter mutation is an interpretation it never tested. Team A said that if so the honest label might be Not verifiable or True, but it answered False anyway. The point was reported, not resolved.

Team B named the same weak point (promoter status depends on the upstream annotation of an alternative transcript) and did not resolve it either, e.g. by checking DISTANCE or that transcript's biotype and strand.
Team A found 0 TERT promoter calls and very few 5'Flank calls, which suggests promoter regions were barely covered. Neither team squared this with claiming a promoter hit.
second_readings: 'Promoter mutation' could mean, strictly, a non-coding variant upstream of the canonical transcription start site. Under that reading a missense change in the canonical coding sequence does not count, and the data may hold no promoter calls at all. Read broadly, it could mean any variant in the 5' regulatory region of any annotated transcript, and then the hotspot counts.

'Absent in desmoplastic melanoma' could mean pure desmoplastic melanoma only, or all desmoplastic melanoma including mixed tumours. The sample-level Pure/Mixed split matters if the hits occur only in mixed tumours.
challenge.verdict: Moderate trust. Both teams found a real recurring hotspot at the 5' end of NFKBIE, but they call it a promoter mutation only by reinterpreting a variant annotated as coding missense on the canonical transcript, and both name this as their weakest, unresolved point. The label depends on whether the variant really is a promoter mutation, and neither team checked that with the annotation columns the data provide.

questions.question: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: For every NFKBIE row, tabulate all_effects per transcript along with DISTANCE, BIOTYPE, CANONICAL and cDNA_position. Does the hotspot lie upstream of, or in the 5'UTR of, the start of a protein-coding NFKBIE transcript, and by how many bases? Does that result change whether you can call it a promoter mutation?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Your weakest point says that if the hotspot is truly coding, the label would be closer to Not verifiable or True, yet you answered False. Which specific check on the data settles this, and once you run it, does your method still lead to the same label?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Report FILTER, Mutation_Status, Validation_Status, t_alt_count/t_depth and n_alt_count/n_depth for each NFKBIE 5'-end call. Do any fail the filters or show alt reads in the normal sample, and does dropping them change your count?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Tabulate Sequence_Source for the NFKBIE calls and for every 5'Flank/upstream call in the MAF. Were promoter-type regions covered in all 20 samples, and does that change how you read the presence or absence of hits?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Your False rests on the upstream_gene_variant annotation of ENST00000477930. Check that transcript's BIOTYPE and strand, and the DISTANCE value in the hotspot rows. Is it a protein-coding transcript that starts near the variant, and does the result change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Count the 5'Flank/upstream calls and the TERT promoter calls in the whole MAF. If promoter regions were barely called, does that change how much weight you give a missense change in the canonical coding sequence as evidence of a promoter mutation?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Report FILTER, Mutation_Status, Validation_Status, t_alt_count/t_depth and n_alt_count for each NFKBIE hit. Do they all pass as somatic, and does dropping any that do not change your result?
QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Split the NFKBIE hits by DETAILED_SAMPLE_HISTOLOGY_CATEGORY (Pure vs Mixed). Are there hits in pure desmoplastic samples, and does the split change your method?
In VEP annotation, how is 'upstream_gene_variant' defined, including its default distance window, and does the term imply that the variant lies in that transcript's promoter?
questions.why: One team's False rests on an upstream_gene_variant annotation on a non-canonical transcript, so whether that annotation implies a promoter location decides the label.

questions.question: In cancer genomics, is a recurrent mutation in the first coding exon or at the 5' end of a gene, within about 100 bp of an alternative transcription start site, usually classified as a promoter mutation or as a coding mutation?
questions.why: Both teams' answer depends on calling a 5'-end hotspot that is coding on the canonical transcript a promoter mutation.

questions.question: Do whole-exome capture kits usually cover gene promoter regions upstream of the transcription start site, and how are such off-target calls usually reported in MAF files (e.g. Variant_Classification 5'Flank)?
questions.why: Decides whether a lack of 5'Flank calls means the mutations are truly absent or the regions were not covered, which bears on True/False versus Not verifiable.

findings.question: In cancer genomics, is a recurrent mutation in the first coding exon or at the 5' end of a gene, within about 100 bp of an alternative transcription start site, usually classified as a promoter mutation or as a coding mutation?
findings.answer: Not settled by the web: all 4 research gateway calls failed (HTTP 502 / Exa 403), so no page was read. Unverified background view: there is no single convention. Standard MAF annotation on the canonical transcript (VEP/Oncotator) labels such a variant by its coding consequence (e.g. Missense/Silent), not 5'Flank/promoter. Element-based noncoding-driver analyses define promoters as windows around the TSS of any annotated transcript, which can overlap 5' coding bases. So calling a 5'-end coding hotspot a 'promoter mutation' is an author's interpretive choice, not a default. The teams should not assume the MAF classes will mark it as promoter, and should say plainly that their label depends on this choice.
